newsitem.title: GERMANY: German officials discuss fate of Bosnian refugees.
newsitem.headline: German officials discuss fate of Bosnian refugees.

text.p: Top officials from Germany's 16 states met federal government officials on Friday to discuss whether to stick to controversial plans to repatriate 315,000 Bosnian refugees by the end of the year.

The states say they cannot afford to keep the refugees much longer but came under pressure this week from politicians in Bonn, refugee agencies and human rights groups not to force the Bosnians to go home too soon.
At the end of the three-hour meeting in Munich, officials said they had reached an agreement which would be handed on to the state interior ministries for approval next week.
"We have agreed on a recommendation on how the problems can be solved," said Gustav Adolf Stange, secretary of state at the interior ministry in Mecklenberg-Vorpommern.
Officials did not say what the proposal was, but hinted the original plans could be interpreted in a flexible way.

"Bavaria will be able to pursue its resolute policy of deportation. The plan allows for the deportation of families from May 1," said Hermann Regensburger, state secretary at the interior ministry in hardline Bavaria.
"But it can allow individual states to set deportations in motion at their own pace," he said.
Critics slammed plans agreed by the states last October to deport refugees who after being served notice refused to leave the country voluntarily, and called on them to revise the plans.

According to phase one of the plan, Germany aims to send 90,000 single adults and married couples without children home by July 1. In phase two of the plan, the rest, refugees with children, would start having to leave from May 1.
Germany's state interior ministries say only around 15,000 Bosnians have gone home of their own accord and that, up to now, about 60 have been deported by Bavaria and Berlin.

A cross-party delegation of Bonn parliamentarians, which visited Bosnia this year, called on the interior ministers of the states on Thursday not to rush as an influx of homeless returnees could aggravate the unstable situation in Bosnia.
It said many refugees who returned had to register with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) because the Bosnian authorities had failed to find them homes.
